# nX-sig commands

<!-- generated by scripts/gen_docs.py from the help
texts of the shell, don't edit it by hand: change the
docstring, then run python scripts/gen_docs.py -->

The commands of the shell (`./nxshell`), the same text
as `help <command>` shows.

Commands are `<action> <object> [arguments]`. The
actions are `ls` (list or show), `add` (save), `rm`
(delete, after confirmation), `run` and `stop`
(background tasks). The object is plural after `ls`
and singular everywhere else: `ls ladders`, but
`rm ladder 1`. An action alone lists its objects.
Keywords with a value, like `count 10 price 20.5`, may
come in either order.

## stocks

```
ls stocks
    count, average buy price and total of
    the stocks you hold, and growth %: how
    far the current price is above (or
    below) the average price
```

## trades

```
ls trades [<stock>]
    the trades of <stock> with their ids
    and its total; without a stock, the
    stocks that have trades

add trade <stock> <buy|sell>
  count <count> price <price>
    record a trade, e.g. 'add trade SOXL
    buy count 10 price 20.5'
add trade from <file>
    record the trades of a bank statement
    csv; fees, stocks not in the config and
    trades already recorded are left out

rm trade <stock> <id>
    delete a trade after confirmation, the
    stock's total is recalculated; the ids
    are in 'ls trades <stock>'
```

## ladders

```
ls ladders
    the saved ladders with their ids, the
    next level they alert at and whether
    they run

add ladder <stock> <down|up> <step>
  from <price> [run]
    save a ladder: a notification each
    time the price moves another <step>
    down (or up) from <price>, e.g. 'add
    ladder SOXL down 10 from 100' at 90,
    80, 70, ...; run starts it right away

rm ladder <id>
    delete a saved ladder after
    confirmation; a running ladder is
    stopped first

run ladder <id> [force]
    start a saved ladder as a background
    process, it keeps running when the
    shell is closed; only one device runs
    the background tasks, force takes them
    over from the other one (when it is off)

stop ladder <id>
    stop a running ladder, it stays saved
```

## rules

```
ls rules
    your personal rules with their ids

add rule <rule>
    save a personal rule, e.g. 'add rule
    never buy on a gap up'

rm rule <id>
    delete a rule after confirmation, the
    rules after it are renumbered
```

## basetrades

```
ls basetrades [sip|iex] [al]
    the basetrades in config order, with
    the current price of each stock and its
    change % from the buying price; sip
    takes the prices from the delayed_sip
    feed, iex from iex (default: config
    "feed"); with al, below it each
    alert's price per stock, a ! when the
    price is past it

add basetrade <stock>|all
    take the basetrade of <stock> from its
    trades: the lowest buy since the last
    sell (a partial sell too), its price
    and count; of two equal buys the later
    one; with all, of each stock that has
    trades, after confirmation if older
    basetrades are replaced
add basetrade <stock> price <price>
  count <count>
    save the last price you bought <stock>
    at and how many, e.g. 'add basetrade
    MRVU price 100 count 10'; replaces the
    stock's older basetrade

rm basetrade <stock>
    delete the basetrade of <stock> after
    confirmation
```

## alerts

```
ls alerts
    the saved alerts and whether the alerts
    process checks them; the levels per
    stock are in 'ls basetrades al'

add alert basetrades <down|up> <n> percent
    a notification each time the price
    of a basetrade's stock crosses <n>
    percent below (down) or above (up) its
    buying price, e.g. 'add alert basetrades
    down 10 percent'; sent again after the
    price went back past the level (by 1%
    of the buying price) and crosses it
    once more. starts the alerts process if
    it isn't running
add alert gain <stock|all> <n> [percent]
    the same for the gain of a held stock
    (or of every one with all), from your
    trades as in xtop: an amount, or a % of
    the average buy price with percent; a
    negative <n> for a loss, e.g. 'add alert
    gain TSMX 100', 'add alert gain all 10
    percent'

rm alert <id>
    delete alert <id> after confirmation;
    the alerts process stops when no alert
    is left

run alerts [force]
    start the alerts process that checks
    every alert (add alert starts it too);
    it keeps running when the shell is
    closed; force takes the background
    tasks over from the other device, see
    'help run ladder'

stop alerts
    stop the alerts process, the alerts
    stay saved
```

## mail-broker

```
run mail-broker [force]
    start the mail broker that records
    broker order emails as trades; it keeps
    running when the shell is closed; force
    takes the background tasks over from the
    other device, see 'help run ladder'

stop mail-broker
    stop the mail broker, after a clean
    logout
```

## web

```
run web
    start the web server that shows the
    nX-sig logo, at config "web" "host" and
    "port" (http://127.0.0.1:8080/ by
    default, only this device); it keeps
    running when the shell is closed

stop web
    stop the web server
```

## tasks

```
ls tasks
    the background tasks that are running
    as their own process, with their pid,
    start time and state, and the device
    that runs them

stop tasks all
    stop every background task running on
    this device: the ladders, the alerts,
    the mail broker and the web server, as
    their own stop commands do; they stay
    saved
```

## other commands

```
status
    show all held positions with count,
    average buy price, current price and
    state: gain/loss in money,
    count * (price - avg price),
    whether the mail broker and the web
    server are running and which device
    runs the background tasks

xtop [sec] [sip|iex] [al]
    live gain/loss of the stocks you hold:
    quantity, average buy price, current
    price, gain and gain %, updated every
    5 seconds or every <sec> seconds,
    e.g. 'xtop 10'; sip takes the prices
    from the delayed_sip feed, iex from iex
    (default: config "feed"); with al,
    below it the gain alerts and the stocks
    in alert (see 'help add alert'). q
    returns to the shell

chart <stock> [period <n> <unit>]
    the price of <stock> over the period
    (5 days by default) as a chart, one *
    per price, with your average buy
    price as a . line and your trades as
    B / S; <unit> is days, weeks or
    months, e.g. 'chart TSMX period 3
    months'

terminal info
    the terminal's size, the width, theme
    and padding in use and where they come
    from,
    the phone or computer model; the width
    and theme are config.json "terminal"
    "width" and "theme"
terminal padding [<spaces>]
    the spaces before each table on this
    device, 0 (default) to 200, e.g.
    'terminal padding 10'; less where a
    table wouldn't fit the width; without
    spaces, the padding now

test notify <alert|ladder> [repeat <n>]
    send a test message like an alert's or
    a ladder's through config.json "notify"
    (telegram, termux or ntfy), to check
    that it arrives. with 'repeat <n>' it
    is sent n times, 5 seconds apart, all
    with the same id: termux and ntfy then
    update one notification, to see how a
    watch shows an updated one

strategy [run/stop/list/get]
    not implemented yet

demo set <stock> <price>
demo move <stock|all> <n>%
demo speed [<n>]
demo reset
demo tour
    only in the demo (./nxdemo): set a
    price, or move one or all by n percent,
    e.g. 'demo move SOXL -5%', to see a
    ladder or an alert send a message;
    speed shows or sets how many times
    faster than real time the prices move;
    reset stops the demo's tasks and starts
    over with the sample data; tour lists
    what to try

help [<command>]
    all commands, or the details of one,
    e.g. 'help add trade', 'help rm' or
    'help ladder'

exit, quit, q
    leave the shell
```
